description.narrative: The Netherlands and Colombia have an agreement cooperation to exchange knowledge and strengthen public health in the Life Sciences and Health Sector (LSH). Colombia has declared cancer as an illness of national priority. The challenge for the country is cantered in integral attention and quality, particularly early detection and screening of breast cancer. The health system in Colombia is largely privatised. 89% of the insurance companies are private and 11% are mixed. 90% of the oncological services are private. The Colombian system lacks standardised procedures and quality control for screening. The main problem is that health providers work under different standards for breast cancer screening. Treatment starts in late stages due to a lack of prompt and quality diagnosis, which increases the mortality rate (mainly of women). The assurance of quality control and screening at the same standard is an imperative need within the health system.The Netherlands has added value by becoming a partner to support Colombia in this challenge. The Netherlands' screening process is one of the most efficient in Europe. Public health institutions execute the screenings in partnership with the Dutch Expert Centre for Screening (LRCB). LRCB is a unique organisation with an integrated approach to quality assurance and quality control of breast cancer screening in the Netherlands and Europe.The project enables the implementation of a site visit of one week by a multidisciplinary team of experts of the LRCB, who will elaborate a detailed baseline assessment of the actual breast cancer screening programme and will provide an advisory report with tailormade recommendations to the National Institute of Cancer of Colombia (INC).
